clue.text: Knock back a shot with backspin, achieving a curve

indicators.note: back says the word for knock is read from right to left

parts.note: to rap is to knock

indicators.note: a ball with backspin travels back, so the word for shot is turned round

parts.note: a lob is a high shot in tennis

explanation.surface: A golfer or tennis player plays a spinning shot that bends through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'with backspin' each turn only the piece beside them; the clue's two a's are each kept as a letter, with 'achieving' merely a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is a particular mathematical curve, the path of a thrown object.

clue.text: Throw up, perhaps, after having two thirds of spud soup

indicators.note: after having puts the reversed piece after the shortened spud
two thirds of the six-letter word for spud keeps its first four letters

parts.note: spud is slang for potato

indicators.note: in a down clue throw up says the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone is sick after eating most of a potato soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thirds of' drops TO from POTATO; 'Throw up' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick French-style soup, a cookery word in English.

clue.text: Legendary twin birds grounded after first shot of rifleman

indicators.note: after says the birds come after that letter
first shot of picks the opening letter of rifleman

parts.note: emus are flightless birds, grounded

explanation.surface: Flightless birds are brought down after a marksman's first shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus's brother, suckled by a wolf in Rome's founding myth.

clue.text: First past the post would surely have been this!

definitions.text: First past the post would surely have been this!

parts.words: First past the post would surely have been this!
parts.note: a racehorse winning the race has been ridden the best, and to bestride a horse is to sit astride it

explanation.surface: A comment on the winning horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as best + ridden: the winner was surely the best-ridden horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of bestride, describing a mount that has been sat astride.

clue.text: Discharge the Pope?

definitions.meaning: an electrical discharge across a gap, as in welding
read as ..., a Roman Catholic, which the Pope is

explanation.surface: A question whether the pontiff can be dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric spark across a gap, and the letters of 'a Roman Catholic' in short.

clue.text: The Messiah at first reluctant to engage cleaner

parts.note: the initials of Jesus Christ, the first letters of his name
loth means unwilling, reluctant to do something

explanation.surface: Christ is unwilling at first to hire a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A J-cloth is a brand of disposable kitchen cloth used for cleaning, familiar in Britain.

clue.text: See 13
Craft of court organisation a pig to swallow?

indicators.note: to swallow says the pig takes the organisation inside it

parts.note: an oinker is a pig, from its grunt
LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, governing body for tennis courts in Britain

explanation.surface: A legal body's procedures are hard to accept, like swallowing a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, so the 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker is a vessel, and craft is a general word for ships or boats.

clue.text: Help to Miss Whiplash's excitement getting out of short one-piece

indicators.note: getting out of here means being outside, so heat goes round the shortened garment

parts.note: heat is passion or excitement

indicators.note: short means the garment's last letter is cut off

parts.note: a dress is a one-piece garment

explanation.surface: A dominatrix called Miss Whiplash gets excited stepping out of a short dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Whiplash' is a stage name, but read 'Help to miss whiplash': a car seat part that avoids the neck injury. 'short' cuts DRESS to DRES.
explanation.definitionFit: The cushion above a car seat stops the head snapping back in a crash, preventing neck injury.

clue.text: Square x

definitions.meaning: ... Square is the famous New York square
the sign x means multiplied by

explanation.surface: A two-word clue that looks like an algebra instruction to square x.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York square takes its name from the newspaper, and x is the multiplication sign.

clue.text: R. Smythe's baby Fitzgerald performed without accompaniment

parts.note: Reg Smythe created the cartoon character Andy Capp, so his brainchild is 'a Capp'
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A cartoonist's child and a jazz singer gave an unaccompanied performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Capp is a long-running British newspaper comic strip by Reg Smythe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term describes singing done with no instruments backing the voices.

clue.text: Got caught

definitions.meaning: got in the sense of understood, grasped
caught in the sense of arrested by police

explanation.surface: A terse report that someone was caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both grasped mentally and arrested, as by police.

clue.text: PAs having a bad day leave without giving notice

parts.note: the Ides of March was the day Caesar was killed, a bad day
to decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly

explanation.surface: Personal assistants after a bad day quit without notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Military assistants to senior officers are personal aides, so PAs fits.

clue.text: Class 'A': good parts — and bad

indicators.note: bad here means spoilt, so the letters are put into a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Class A drug is described as having good and bad aspects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles A, GOOD and PARTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological class of snails and slugs.

clue.text: This criminal can't argue with getting year: I'll come back clean and corrected

definitions.text: I'll come back clean and corrected

parts.note: a caught crook concedes 'it's a fair cop', an admission he was justly arrested

explanation.surface: A crook accepts his year's sentence and vows to return reformed and going straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat final version of a document, without errors, returned after editing.

clue.text: Openers batting after lunch? Supporting the flipping game, one had Duckworth-Lewis discounted

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: discounted means not counted, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: tiddlywinks is played by flipping small discs into a cup
I'd is a contraction of I had, and I is one
DL, the Duckworth-Lewis method for rain-affected cricket matches

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: openers bat after lunch, and the Duckworth-Lewis rain rule is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'openers' are eyelids, and 'batting' means blinking, as after a heavy lunch. 'discounted' removes the letters for 'one had' and Duckworth-Lewis, which sit together in the game's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nap, when the eyelids flutter shut, often taken after a meal.

clue.text: Poor dad's so broke it might come in useful

indicators.note: poor here means in a bad state, so the letters are made to come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A penniless father finds something that might help him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DADSSOBROKE; the S of 'dad's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, cryptic description of a book of contacts' details, handy to have.

clue.text: In my own time, I adapted this for retail use

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of retail use come from a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone says they modified this for shops in their spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things without hurry, whenever convenient, is doing them in one's own time.

clue.text: Strike's success

definitions.meaning: to strike is to give a blow
a popular song or show is a smash

explanation.surface: A strike action that turns out well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a blow and a popular success go by the same short word.

clue.text: Ring around to engage thatcher to write off Teri's roof

indicators.note: around says the ring goes round the other letters

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
to engage someone is to use them, employ them

indicators.note: write off means remove, so the actress's surname is taken out of the word

parts.note: Teri Hatcher, the American actress from Desperate Housewives

explanation.surface: A ring is placed round a hired thatcher to fix Teri's roof.
explanation.walkthrough: THATCHER less HATCHER (Teri Hatcher's surname) leaves just T.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a house, its roof, is literally its housetop.

clue.text: Patient's conclusion following City 'treatment'?

indicators.note: following puts the patient's last letter after the City letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

indicators.note: conclusion picks the final letter of the word patient

explanation.surface: A patient's verdict on the treatment received at a city hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Electroconvulsive therapy is a psychiatric treatment known by its initials.

clue.text: Polygraph's electrode might need tightening with it

indicators.note: a loose electrode needs fixing, so its letters with those of it are loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A polygraph's electrode may come loose and need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might need tightening' says ELECTRODE and IT are loose, so their letters are rearranged; the 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph is the machine used to test whether someone is telling the truth.

clue.text: Confine broadcasts sequentially

indicators.note: broadcasts signals a word as spoken on the air

parts.note: sequentially means one after another, in turn

explanation.surface: Programmes are transmitted one after another under restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern people is to confine them, as enemy aliens in wartime.

clue.text: Nanny's quickly turned over Viz feature about foremost of sexists

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the reversed feature goes round a letter
turned over says the Viz feature is read backwards

parts.note: Top Tips is a long-running reader-tips page in the British comic Viz

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of sexists

explanation.surface: A nanny hastily flips through a sexist adult comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes SPITPOT, and 'about' puts S (first of sexists) inside it. Viz is a crude British humour magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Poppins, the fictional nanny, says the phrase to mean hurry up, at once.

clue.text: We maidens love scheming

indicators.note: scheming means plotting, so the letters are plotted into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Young women declare their delight in plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheming' rearranges WEMAIDENS with O; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who devise plans would say they love scheming, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Love in extra's heart for actress

indicators.note: in places the letter for love within the word for extra, at its heart

parts.note: more means extra, additional
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love lies at the heart of a film extra's hopes of being an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' says the O goes in the middle of MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi Moore or Julianne Moore are both well-known film actresses.

clue.text: See 20
Unscrupulously put forward and back, I left secure banks

indicators.note: banks means lines the sides of, so the trimmed word encloses the back
left means departed, so the letter I goes from the word

parts.note: to tie up is to secure
the rump is the back end of an animal

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling to and fro has secured the river banks after I departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the animal's hindquarters, not a reversal signal; 'left' drops the I, and 'banks' means the trimmed word lines both sides of the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges that are fabricated are said to be invented and advanced dishonestly.

clue.text: Yorkshire banker going after 4dn 16ac 17ac in buildings?

indicators.note: going after means what follows the three cross-referenced answers within the word for buildings

parts.note: architecture is the body of buildings of a place or style
the answers to 4-down, 16-across and 17-across put together

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire banker comes after some cross-referenced answers in property dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, something with banks. 'going after' says the answer is what follows the three cross-referenced answers, run together, in the word for buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, flowing through Wensleydale.

clue.text: Just like the Piggy-wig, the Turkey tied it!

definitions.text: Just like the Piggy-wig, the Turkey tied it!

parts.words: Just like the Piggy-wig, the Turkey tied it!
parts.note: in Lear's The Owl and the Pussy-cat the Piggy-wig has a ring at the end of his nose and the Turkey marries the couple

explanation.surface: A nod to Lear's nonsense poem, where a turkey ties the knot.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring (O) in a nose is the Piggy-wig's look, and a tied loop is what the Turkey ties: the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope tied with a running knot, the kind of knot one ties.

clue.text: Quite 13

definitions.meaning: rather or fairly, as in 'rather good'
refers to the 13-across answer's first word, meaning good-looking or attractive

explanation.surface: A bare two-word clue: 'quite' plus a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning rather and as an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: Heinz's bar order is 'Genius'?

parts.note: a German, Heinz, ordering in a bar asks for one beer mug in German, ..., which sounds like the physicist's name

explanation.surface: A German drinker's order at the bar is apparently a stroke of brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used to mean any genius, and in German it splits as 'a beer mug'.
